card.summary: BedrockTogether lets you join any Bedrock Edition server from Minecraft on Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch - no PC and no DNS changes required.

free_tier.stated: BedrockTogether lets you join any Bedrock Edition server from Minecraft on Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch - no PC and no DNS changes required.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published and none applies: the app runs on the player's phone and the vendor carries nothing.; ingress: none

record.interface_detail: A mobile app with a three-step join flow.
record.chaining: Sits in front of whatever UDP path the host already has; adds none.
record.binding_note: The app is a LAN bridge on the player's phone, so no host gets a public endpoint and no quota is ever met.

identity_cost.detail: No account: an App Store or Play Store install.

record.reliability_note: The phone must stay on the same network as the console for the LAN method; the Switch needs the Xbox Live broadcast method instead.
record.confidence_note: The page states the mechanism plainly; whether the app also offers a hosted relay mode is not stated and was not tested.

evidence.proved: 'BedrockTogether runs on your phone and puts any Bedrock server in front of your console - no PC, no DNS rerouting, no router settings.'
'BedrockTogether makes any Minecraft Bedrock Edition server appear as a LAN game on Xbox, PlayStation & Nintendo Switch.'

record.notes: Mobile proxy application that connects to remote Minecraft Bedrock servers and re-broadcasts them as local LAN games. Operates client-side on local devices rather than providing a hosted public UDP endpoint.

extras.wg_detail: No WireGuard; the app proxies on the player's own network.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published and none applies: the app runs on the player's phone and the vendor carries nothing.
extras.transit_note: Player traffic goes phone to server; the app is a local relay on the player side.
